quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q4 2026 (June quarter) results: CEO Stephen Chang said revenue came in above the midpoint of guidance; as anticipated, strength in Advanced Computing (particularly AI and server applications) and in the Communications segment offset softness in the traditional PC market, driven by higher memory costs, and in Gaming within Consumer. CFO Yifan Liang: DMOS revenue was $113.2 million (down 1.6% sequentially, up 5.6% over last year); Power IC revenue was $55.5 million (up 18.2% from the prior quarter, down 19.3% from a year ago); assembly service and other revenue was $1.7 million (vs $1.9 million last quarter and $0.5 million a year ago). Non-GAAP gross margin was 23.7% vs 21.7% last quarter and 24.4% a year ago, the quarter-over-quarter increase mainly from better mix and higher utilization; non-GAAP operating expenses were $45.3 million (vs $44.3 million prior quarter and $40.9 million last year), up mainly on higher R&D; non-GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.13 (vs a loss of $0.28 last quarter and earnings of $0.02 a year ago). Operating cash flow was negative $10 million; EBITDA excluding equity method investment income and loss was $10.1 million (vs $5.9 million last quarter and $10.5 million a year ago); cash ended at $180.8 million (vs $190.3 million). Days sales outstanding were 23 days (vs 20 days); average days in inventory were 138 days (vs 139 days).
quarterly_data.figure: June-quarter revenue $170.4 million (down 3.5% year over year, up 4% sequentially); DMOS $113.2 million; Power IC $55.5 million; non-GAAP gross margin 23.7% (21.7% prior quarter, 24.4% a year ago); non-GAAP EPS loss $0.13; cash $180.8 million; inventory days 138

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Segment results for the June quarter (CEO Stephen Chang): Computing was down 8.6% year over year and up 5.6% sequentially at about 49.8% of revenue, at the high end of guidance for a low- to mid-single-digit sequential increase; Advanced Computing increased 35% sequentially and was a record high 31% of the Computing segment, driven by AI, server, workstation and cloud applications, while declines in PCs, tablets and graphics cards offset it. Consumer was down 21.3% year over year and up 8% sequentially (12.3% of revenue), better than the expected flattish quarter with quarter-on-quarter growth across Gaming, Wearables and Home Appliances; the year-over-year decline mainly reflects lower Gaming revenue as the current console product cycle nears maturity. Communications was up 22.3% year over year and down 2.3% sequentially (19.3% of revenue), as seasonally lower battery PCM shipments ahead of new smartphone model transitions were largely offset by strong growth in DC-DC modules and networking applications. Power Supply and Industrial was 17.6% of revenue, up 1.4% year over year and 5.2% sequentially, driven by E-Mobility and DC fans tied to AI server demand, partially offset by declines in Quick Chargers and AC-DC power supplies.
quarterly_data.figure: Computing -8.6% YoY / +5.6% QoQ, about 49.8% of revenue; Advanced Computing +35% QoQ, record 31% of Computing; Consumer -21.3% YoY / +8% QoQ, 12.3%; Communications +22.3% YoY / -2.3% QoQ, 19.3%; Power Supply and Industrial +1.4% YoY / +5.2% QoQ, 17.6%

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AI and server ramp (CEO Stephen Chang): for the September quarter AOS expects Advanced Computing revenue to grow by more than 40% sequentially, driven by AI servers, graphics cards and other high-performance computing platforms; the AI and server business alone is expected to increase more than 60% sequentially and represent the majority of Advanced Computing, and Advanced Computing is expected to exceed 40% of Computing segment revenue and approach 20% of total company revenue. Demand for the medium-voltage MOSFET portfolio 'continues to expand across AI and cloud infrastructure with growing engagement from power supply providers, module makers, leading ODMs, cloud service providers, and hyperscale customers', and he expects these products to contribute more meaningfully during the second half of 2026 and into 2027. The growth is 'a combination of ramping previous sockets and new program traction' across a more diversified customer base, with programs going into hyperscalers and into power supplies for data centers. Several products were released late last calendar year or at the beginning of this calendar year and the ramp 'really started around the March quarter'; the high-performance and medium-voltage MOSFETs sold into these applications face less competition and command better pricing and margin. AOS continues expanding its medium-voltage manufacturing capacity while increasing targeted R&D investments for next-generation AI infrastructure.
quarterly_data.figure: September quarter: Advanced Computing up more than 40% sequentially; AI and server up more than 60% sequentially; Advanced Computing to exceed 40% of Computing and approach 20% of total revenue

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: September-quarter guidance (CFO Yifan Liang): revenue approximately $176 million plus or minus $10 million; GAAP gross margin 23.8% plus or minus 1%; non-GAAP gross margin 24.5% plus or minus 1%; GAAP operating expenses $52.5 million and non-GAAP $46.5 million, each plus or minus $1 million; interest income $0.6 million higher than interest expense; income tax expense $1.1 million to $1.3 million. The CFO said the guidance is another 70 to 80 basis points of gross margin improvement, primarily from better product mix, and factors in some impact from the typhoon on the back-end factory. By segment (CEO Stephen Chang): Computing flattish sequentially as Advanced Computing growth more than offsets weakness in traditional PC applications caused by memory chip constraints; Consumer down approximately 25% sequentially (lower Home Appliances, Wearables and Gaming); Communications up approximately 10% sequentially as AOS ramps new products with its Tier 1 U.S. smartphone customer; Power Supply and Industrial up nearly 30% sequentially on stronger Power Tools demand, continued momentum in DC fans supporting AI server rack applications, and sequential increases in Quick Chargers and AC-DC power supplies.
quarterly_data.figure: September-quarter revenue approximately $176 million plus or minus $10 million; GAAP gross margin 23.8% +/- 1%; non-GAAP gross margin 24.5% +/- 1%; GAAP opex $52.5 million, non-GAAP opex $46.5 million (+/- $1 million); Consumer down approximately 25%, Communications up approximately 10%, Power Supply and Industrial up nearly 30% sequentially

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Typhoon disruption and capacity (CEO Stephen Chang, CFO Yifan Liang): a couple of days before the call, Shanghai experienced Typhoon Dolphin and flooding that impacted portions of AOS's packaging operations; the CEO expects 'a slight impact to the September quarter' and said teams are moving quickly to restore effective capacity, minimize customer disruption and recover as much of the delayed business as possible in the coming quarters. The CFO said the initial assessment is an impact 'in the range of a few million dollars, with some effect on margins', reflected in the September guidance. June-quarter CapEx was $14.9 million vs $12.1 million the prior quarter, and September-quarter CapEx is expected at $15 million to $17 million; AOS is expanding manufacturing capacity in key product areas, including medium-voltage capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: typhoon impact in the range of a few million dollars; CapEx $14.9 million (vs $12.1 million prior quarter); September-quarter CapEx $15 million to $17 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 800-volt timing (CEO Stephen Chang): 'We're a little early to forecast that precisely. We do see 800-volt solutions approaching and we are promoting our solutions for those applications. I wouldn't be surprised if we see some business next year, but it likely will be a transition rather than an immediate material shift.' Standard 48-volt platforms are still prevalent and will coexist for a while; when 800-volt adoption ramps, AOS expects to be ready with new solutions, phased in alongside other programs.

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Gross margin drivers and pricing: CFO Yifan Liang said June-quarter gross margin improved from the March quarter by 200 basis points, a slightly larger portion from product mix and a smaller portion from utilization and operating expense changes. CEO Stephen Chang said the Advanced Computing mix shift, 'combined with an improving pricing environment, is expected to support higher gross margins in the second half of calendar 2026', and that growth in high-performance applications combined with better mix should support margin improvement in the second half of the calendar year; AI and server products are becoming a larger proportion of both the Computing segment and the overall company and are 'accretive to our margin'.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin up 200 basis points from the March quarter

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Memory shortage impact on PCs, graphics and smartphones (CEO Stephen Chang): standard PCs grew modestly in the June quarter from March, but AOS expects an adjustment in the September quarter as end customers face memory and CPU shortages; 'We mainly see September as the main correction. The December quarter is still unclear, and we're not expecting a correction at this point, but we will need to see how the memory situation evolves.' In graphics there are no major platform releases this year; AOS expects the next platform release sometime next year and will prioritize it for growth. In smartphones, AOS is focused on premium platforms with its Tier 1 U.S. customer, where battery protection solutions and support for higher charging currents are increasing BOM content; outside the premium tier, elevated memory pricing and supply constraints are pushing some OEMs toward lower performance components in certain platforms, and AOS is 'preparing for a growth season for our battery PCM business'. He said he believes the Computing and Communications businesses are outperforming their respective end markets.

quarterly_data.quarter: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D investment (CFO Yifan Liang, CEO Stephen Chang): AOS has been ramping hiring and investment in R&D, primarily for AI and total solutions for PC and smartphone areas; with positions still being filled there may be modest additional growth into the December quarter, but the most significant ramp in R&D headcount and spending is expected to occur this year. The CEO said AOS is 'in an investment mode' and expects next year to be 'more standard organic growth rather than another stepped-up increase'.
